exposure: Type of prenatal care provider (physician vs. midwife)
outcome: Interference of childbirth fear with daily functioning
cohort: A total of 409 Canadian pregnant women participated in an online survey about their current and previous pregnancy experiences.
finding: Different dimensions of childbirth fear are associated with preferences for place and mode of birth, type of care provider, and satisfaction with care among Canadian women.
mod_finding: Women preferring cesarean birth were more fearful of pain, loss of sexual pleasure/attractiveness, and harm, and reported more interference with daily functioning, whereas women preferring vaginal birth were more fearful of interventions.
